hints.title: Directed Graph from Precedence Pairs
hints.text: Each adjacent pair in sequences defines a directed edge representing necessary relative ordering between elements.

hints.title: Uniqueness Requires Single Candidate Queue
hints.text: For the shortest common supersequence to be unique, the zero in-degree candidate collection must contain exactly one element at every topological step.

hints.title: Kahn Algorithm with Single Element Queue Invariant
hints.text: Build adjacency graph and in-degree counts from sequences. Enqueue nodes with in-degree 0. At each step, if queue size is not 1, return false. Check that popped element matches nums[step].

hints.title: See the blueprint

variables: V: number of nodes in nums
E: total number of sequence edges
complexity.notes: Optimal topological sort running in linear O(V + E) time and space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing all possible permutations or sub-sequences is factorial O(N!).
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Kahn algorithm validates both topological existence and strict path uniqueness.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that uniqueness of topological sort requires queue length strictly 1 at each step.
